answer: We establish a mechanism where dynamic opportunity-cost bonds require validators to deposit saffron-weighted staking collateral into a cryptographic trellis that tracks state transitions. Deviation triggers a subgame-perfect slashing matrix executing zero-knowledge verifiable delays, rendering the expected payoff of identity multiplication strictly negative and hollowing out any Sybil incentive. Consequently, rational adversaries abandon identity fragmentation, forcing convergence to a unique, robust Nash equilibrium in multi-agent environments.
